name: mid-block
reply:
What I saw
- The coach requested an 11v11 setup showing our ATT 4-2-3-1 against a DEF 4-4-2 mid-block in the middle third.
- The current board featured a 4-3-3 shape which we are adjusting to align with our club's double-pivot build-out model.

On the board
- Placed our ATT 4-2-3-1 in possession with a split centre-back pairing and a double pivot (#6 and #8) providing a secure central platform.
- Set up the opponent in a compact 4-4-2 mid-block within the middle third to deny central penetration.
- Added tactical pass and movement arrows to highlight the #10 pocket and wide support angles.

Coaching points
- In possession, prioritize ball security and maintain positional support so the ball-carrier always has a safe option and a line-breaking option.
- Use the double pivot to secure the center and liberate our fullbacks high and wide for width.
- Recognize when the opponent's block is narrow, and use a switch of play or third-man combination to break pressure.
